purpose: Proposed display curation for the next author audit; no removals are applied.

groups.title: Named-reference occurrence bars
groups.reason: The same displayed count pattern appears in both presentations. Keep the specifically described cohort view; move the other presentation out of the main browse view. This is a visual redundancy recommendation, not a new numerical-equivalence finding.

groups.title: Named-reference time traces
groups.reason: The two filled traces look nearly identical. Prefer the explicitly described quench-cohort card; retain the alternate and its provenance in the full library.

groups.title: Total-size string-variety histogram
groups.reason: Both captions describe the full 10,259,647-string union and the same 1–92-atom range/mode. Prefer the annotated mode presentation.

groups.title: Recurrence presentations
groups.reason: Both captions state the same carbon-string recurrence summary. Use one primary presentation; keep the alternate available for detailed review.

groups.title: Local motif comparisons
groups.reason: The state-weighting definitions differ. Prefer the both-state view for browsing; retain the original-weight variant as a specialist companion. These are not numerically interchangeable.

groups.title: Mean-fragment trace alternatives
groups.reason: Two historical presentations occupy separate cards. Prefer the revised view for browsing; keep source/sampling qualifications accessible. Do not infer identical reductions from visual similarity.

groups.title: Quench mean/maximum companions
groups.reason: The four-panel overview carries the mean and maximum comparison. Move the single-statistic/density companions into an expandable group unless they answer a specific discussion question; their plotting/statistical views remain distinct.

groups.title: Additional historical largest-fragment trace
groups.reason: Keep both author-requested dense and sparse products. The extra blue historical rendering can move out of the main view; no equivalence of the dense and sparse products is implied.

groups.title: Dense-system renderings
groups.reason: The initial/after pair supplies a clear comparison. The two dense close/head-on renderings add less at thumbnail size and can move to a development-system detail group.

groups.title: Historical named-query violins
groups.reason: The lower-count views are visually close. Prefer one browse card and retain the other as an alternate. Figure 97 uses a different count scale and is deliberately not called a duplicate; review its definition separately.
